blocks.text: 1. Top-p Sampling
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293136-948383987.png

Top-k Sampling's own closing recap, already covered in Top-k Sampling, pointed forward here. Top-p Sampling, which adapts its cutoff to the shape of each distribution instead, refines the same general truncation idea.
It is genuinely also called nucleus sampling, choosing words by cumulative probability rather than a fixed count, a mechanism explored in full throughout this topic.
2. Recapping The Preview

This connects back to Top-k Sampling's own closing recap, already covered in Top-k Sampling. Top-p sampling was genuinely previewed there as addressing top-k's own fixed-count limitation, briefly described in that earlier topic.
This topic genuinely gives it the complete, dedicated treatment already promised, exploring every detail already hinted at generally in that earlier topic.
3. Recapping The Fixed K Limitation
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293137-75094904.png

This connects back to fixed k across varying distributions, already covered in Top-k Sampling. A genuinely fixed count of words genuinely means something very different across a sharp distribution and a flat one.
Top-p sampling genuinely replaces that fixed count with a genuinely adaptive, probability-based cutoff instead, the core idea explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 4. Cumulative Probability Mass
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293138-832296754.png
This connects back to recapping the fixed k limitation, already covered in this topic. Words genuinely get sorted from most to least likely, then genuinely added up one at a time.
That genuinely running total is exactly what gets called cumulative probability mass, the exact core quantity explored throughout the rest of this topic.
5. The P Cutoff Threshold
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293138-686647822.png
This connects back to cumulative probability mass, already covered in this topic. Words genuinely keep getting added until that genuinely running total first reaches a chosen threshold p.
Only that genuinely smallest set of words reaching threshold p actually stays in the candidate pool, the exact stopping rule explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This stopping rule, already covered in this topic, directly explains why top-p sampling is also genuinely called nucleus sampling, referring to that small nucleus of words carrying most of the probability mass.

blocks.text: 6. Adaptive Candidate Set Size
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293139-278110056.png
This connects back to the p cutoff threshold, already covered in this topic. A genuinely sharp, confident distribution genuinely needs very few words to reach threshold p.
A genuinely flat, uncertain distribution genuinely needs many more words to reach that exact same threshold p, the genuinely key adaptive behavior explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This adaptive behavior, already covered in this topic, directly solves the fixed k limitation already covered in Top-k Sampling, since the candidate pool size now genuinely responds to how confident the model actually is at each step.

blocks.text: 7. Renormalizing Top-p Candidates

This connects back to adaptive candidate set size, already covered in this topic. Just like top-k sampling, already covered in Top-k Sampling, the remaining candidate probabilities genuinely get renormalized.
This happens so sampling among them still genuinely behaves like a genuinely proper probability distribution, a genuinely necessary technical detail explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 8. Choosing A P Value
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293140-160927863.png
This connects back to renormalizing top-p candidates, already covered in this topic. A genuinely lower p value genuinely keeps a smaller, more conservative candidate pool.
A genuinely higher p value genuinely keeps a larger, more permissive candidate pool instead, a genuinely real, tunable tradeoff explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Top-p sampling, also called nucleus sampling, chooses words by cumulative probability, not a fixed count.
It replaces top-k sampling's fixed word count with an adaptive, probability-based cutoff.
Words are sorted from most to least likely and added up until reaching threshold p.
Only that smallest set of words reaching threshold p stays in the candidate pool.
A sharp, confident distribution needs few words to reach p; a flat one needs many more.
Remaining candidate probabilities get renormalized so sampling stays a proper distribution.
A lower p value keeps a smaller pool; a higher p value keeps a larger, more permissive one.
Top-p sampling adapts naturally across varying distributions, unlike top-k's fixed count.
